statement_en: That independently evolved gliding lineages converge at the sequence level at protein-interface positions: some interface position carries, in gliders, a residue not found in non-gliders.
reason_detail: Zero of 532 experimental interface positions separate gliders from non-gliders. Every interface position tested carries, in gliders, a residue also found in non-gliders. The whole-alignment companion test is worse than a null: 11 glider-convergent columns against 17 for a ROLE-SWAPPED baseline, so gliders do not resemble each other more than they resemble other lineages' non-gliders. Identity follows ancestry, not gliding.
what_was_tried: 532 experimental interface positions across 6 deposited structures, with 3-5 independent gliding lineages each (nine Exocoetidae counted as ONE lineage, two flying halfbeaks, the sugar glider, two colugos, a parachute gecko), each with matched non-gliding controls.

A stated separation rule: a column separates gliders only when every glider residue differs from every non-glider residue, at least two independent gliding lineages carry the glider residue, and at least five non-gliders are scored. Result: 0 of 532.
A whole-alignment version over nine fin genes with a role-swapped baseline: 11 glider-convergent columns vs 17 baseline columns.
An earlier UniProt-based version of the same test was run, found worthless, and discarded rather than reported.
what_survives: The null is real within its stated limits, and the limits are recorded rather than glossed: a gap column counts as a gap and not a difference; tblastn projections are excluded; the structures are human and mouse, so every fish, reptile and amphibian residue is reached by a cross-species jump; and interface membership is a 4.0 A cutoff in ONE deposited conformation, so a residue just outside the cutoff, or one that only contacts its partner in another state, counts as non-interface here. What also survives is a self-correction worth more than the null: an earlier version of this test produced "10 interface positions separating gliders" from a single low-identity, name-matched colugo sequence, and the thread caught and discarded it rather than publishing it. And the one real convergence this project holds -- lat4a F326L in flying fishes and gliding halfbeaks -- survives untouched; it simply does not extend to mammals, and it sits 20 A from the substrate site with no transport assay in any species.
sources: Daane JM et al. 2021, Curr Biol, PMID 34534441

evidence.claim: The headline null, with the panel and the rule.
evidence.quote: **532 experimental interface positions, 6 structures, 3-5 independent gliding lineages each - zero positions separate gliders from non-gliders.** Every interface position tested carries, in gliders, a residue also found in non-gliders.
evidence.kind: computed null over fetched alignments and deposited structures

evidence.claim: The role-swapped baseline makes it worse than a null.
evidence.quote: Across the nine fin genes, 11 alignment columns show a residue shared by gliders of two or more lineages and absent from their non-gliding relatives, against 17 columns for the role-swapped baseline. ... Gliders do not resemble each other more than they resemble other lineages' non-gliders (see mean_identity_cross_lineage): identity follows ancestry, not gliding.
evidence.kind: computed metric with a role-swapped negative control

evidence.claim: The discarded earlier version, recorded by the thread itself.
evidence.quote: My own UniProt-based version of this test was worthless and I nearly reported it: only **one** glider (the colugo) had any sequence, so the "10 interface positions separating gliders" it first produced were one low-identity, name-matched sequence differing from everything else. An identity gate (>= 50 %) cut that to one position, and even that is a single-lineage artifact.

found_by: Harvested from structures/README.md and sequences/gliders.json. NOTE a mis-citation found while harvesting: sim-engine/validate/functional/analogue.mjs:3-8 describes this result as "0 of 532 interface positions shared across gliding taxa", but the finding is that 0 of 532 SEPARATE gliders from non-gliders; interfaces-across-lineages.json records positions_shared: 532, the opposite number. The comment understates the panel and misstates the metric. Not corrected here: that file belongs to the validate thread, and this record is the hook for it.

scope_note: Static mirror of lean/registry/open-questions/. An OPEN QUESTION is a question this project holds unsettled, with an arm per live position, each arm's evidence quoted from its primary source, and a belief `proportion` COMPUTED by pipeline/leanbio/belief.mjs rather than asserted. A proportion orders the arms; it is NOT a probability that an arm is true, and belief-params.json says plainly that its parameters are hand-set and not fitted. No arm of an open question is in any law set, and the guard in openq-lib.mjs refuses to accept a law that asserts one. A FAILED THEOREM is a statement this project tried and could not establish, kept with its reason so nobody reproposes it; `what_survives` says what is still true after the failure. Arms formalised in Lean are proved internally consistent and are NOT proved true of any organism.
